elections.stakes: PM Andris Kulbergs's centre-right United List won a record victory, keeping a firmly pro-Ukraine government in a NATO frontline state, while Russia-friendly populist parties gained in the east.

elections.dateNote: Presidency: Bećirović (Bosniak), Cvijanović (Serb), Filipovic (Croat)
elections.stakes: Record-low turnout returned largely familiar ethnic parties; Dodik's SNSD kept control in Republika Srpska, sustaining secessionist pressure that tests the Dayton settlement and the EU path.
elections.winner: Presidency: Denis Bećirović, Željka Cvijanović, Darijana Filipovic

elections.dateNote: No majority: runoff on 25 Oct between Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula
elections.seats: President, 513 Chamber of Deputies seats, 54 of 81 Senate seats
elections.stakes: Latin America's largest economy split almost evenly between Lula's left and the Bolsonaro right, with implications for Amazon policy, BRICS and relations with Washington.

elections.dateNote: Single-round vote; no runoff. RIK preliminary results adopted 26 Oct gave 140 and 104 seats; CeSID-Ipsos projection gave 141 and 103. SPS list (Factor of Stabil
elections.stakes: After nearly two years of student-led protests, the Student List won an outright majority, ending the Serbian Progressive Party's 14 years in power. The result will shape Serbia's balance between the EU and Russia.

elections.dateNote: Runoff held 25 Oct; first round 4 Oct, where Flávio Bolsonaro led Lula by over 2.2 million votes
elections.stakes: The runoff decided whether Lula would win a fourth term or the Bolsonaro family would return to power, a choice with implications for Brazil's climate, trade and foreign-policy direction.

elections.dateNote: Vote held 27 Oct 2026; final results published 30 Oct; results submitted to President 4 Nov; no bloc reached 61 seats; Knesset to be sworn in 10 Nov
elections.stakes: First general election since the 7 October 2023 attack and the Gaza war; no bloc reached the 61-seat majority, with Netanyahu's bloc on 53 seats, so coalition talks will decide whether he keeps power.

elections.dateNote: Runoff 1 Nov 2026 after 1st round 25 Oct (Yotova 34.8%, Gyurov 31.9%; turnout 22.98%). Runoff turnout 28.67%. Final CEC results 2 Nov
elections.stakes: Acting president Iliana Yotova, backed by Progressive Bulgaria, won the runoff against Andrey Gyurov, who had pro-Western opposition backing. Observers read the result as a test of Bulgaria's stance on Russia and Ukraine.

contenders.name: Andrey Gyurov
contenders.leader: Independent (We Continue the Change, Democratic Bulgaria)

elections.dateNote: Vote held Tue 3 Nov. Democrats won control of the House (AP, 12 Nov: 255 D, 169 R, some races uncalled) and the Senate (AP, 9 Nov: 54 D, 44 R; Alaska and Missis
elections.stakes: Control of Congress for the second half of Donald Trump's term, deciding how much of his agenda on tariffs, immigration and spending can pass.

elections.dateNote: Preliminary count 7 Nov; about 399,000 special votes still being counted; official results 27 Nov; caretaker government until then
elections.stakes: The preliminary count gives the National-led coalition 67 of 131 seats, one above the 66 needed. About 400,000 special votes, which have historically leaned left, are still being counted, so the government is not yet settled.

elections.dateNote: Called by Pedro Sánchez on 5 Oct 2026 via Royal Decree 806/2026; date confirmed for 29 Nov
elections.stakes: Sánchez called an early vote after Congress rejected his housing decrees. Polls point to a PP-led government that would need Vox, bringing the far right into government in a major EU economy.

elections.dateNote: Four federal questions on one ballot
elections.stakes: Voters decide on a 0.4-point VAT rise to help fund the 13th pension, looser war-materiel export rules for partner states in conflict, a fireworks restriction and joint taxation of married couples.

elections.dateNote: Set by acting president Čupić on 24 Nov; must be held by 27 Dec 2026
elections.stakes: Vučić resigned to run for prime minister, forcing an early presidential vote on 27 December, held separately from the 25 October parliamentary election. The Student List has a candidate, while the SNS has not yet confirmed one, so the result will show whether the presidency stays with the ruling camp.

contenders.name: Student movement candidate (name not yet disclosed)

elections.dateNote: Earliest possible date; not yet confirmed, pending validation of signatures
elections.stakes: Voters would decide whether to lift the ban on building new nuclear power plants, which parliament approved in June 2026. Supporters cite winter electricity security and climate goals; opponents cite cost, radioactive waste and the growth of renewables.

elections.dateNote: Advance voting 1–6 Mar 2027
elections.stakes: Isamaa leads the latest polling trend ahead of the Centre Party, while Prime Minister Kristen Michal's Reform Party has fallen to about 13 percent. The result could bring a change of government in this NATO frontline state bordering Russia.

elections.dateNote: Due 2027, four years after April 2023; date not set
elections.stakes: Elects the 28-member General Council, which then elects the head of government. The current government is led by Xavier Espot Zamora of Democrats for Andorra.

elections.dateNote: Runoff 2 May 2027
elections.stakes: With Emmanuel Macron barred from a third term, the far-right National Rally leads every poll, raising the prospect of a eurosceptic president with control of a nuclear power's foreign policy.
The opposition Social Democrats lead over PM Petteri Orpo's coalition, which includes the nationalist Finns Party; NATO's newest frontline member with Russia faces a likely change of government.

elections.dateNote: PM says spring 2027; legal deadline 25 Jul 2027
elections.stakes: Kyriakos Mitsotakis seeks a third term but New Democracy polls near 30%, short of a majority, while Alexis Tsipras's new left party has become the main challenger.

elections.dateNote: Due by 30 Jun 2027; date not set
elections.stakes: Montenegro, a leading EU accession candidate, votes in a contest between PM Milojko Spajić's Europe Now! and rival blocs, including the former ruling DPS and the pro-Serbian For the Future of Montenegro.

elections.dateNote: Planned for June 2027; date not yet set by Federal Council
elections.stakes: Voters decide whether to approve the Bilaterals III package of updated and new EU agreements, including rules on free movement of people and dispute settlement. Approval would shape Switzerland's relationship with the EU for the next decade.

elections.dateNote: Usually first half of June; exact date not set
elections.stakes: Incumbent Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh is term-limited; the race between the ruling MPP and the Democratic Party sets the tone for Mongolia's democracy sandwiched between Russia and China.

elections.dateNote: Election day; no runoff
elections.stakes: First midterm test for President Claudia Sheinbaum; Morena and allies seek to keep their supermajority in the Chamber of Deputies. The vote also covers 17 governorships and thousands of local posts.

elections.dateNote: Date set by parliament speaker; term expires autumn 2027
elections.stakes: Liberal Progressive Slovakia narrowly leads Robert Fico's Smer, whose government has softened support for Ukraine and clashed with Brussels over rule of law; the result shapes Slovakia's alignment with Hungary.

elections.dateNote: Due by 11 Nov 2027; President sets date (Oct-Nov Sundays/holidays)
elections.stakes: Donald Tusk's pro-EU coalition leads but may lack a majority, while a combined right including two far-right Confederations could return; key for Ukraine support and EU rule-of-law politics.

elections.dateNote: Must be held by 22 Dec 2027; exact date not confirmed
elections.stakes: Giorgia Meloni seeks re-election after a full term; polls show her Brothers of Italy leading but a combined centre-left ahead of the centre-right coalition.

elections.dateNote: Autumn 2027 (October); exact date not set; runoff if needed
elections.stakes: Incumbent liberal independent Nataša Pirc Musar is eligible for a second term but undeclared; former president Borut Pahor has not ruled out a return.

elections.seats: 200 National Council + 46 Council of States seats
elections.stakes: The national-conservative SVP is polling near 30%; the election comes as Switzerland debates ratifying a new treaty package with the EU, which the SVP opposes.

elections.dateNote: Runoff within 30 days if needed, likely 21 Nov 2027
elections.stakes: Javier Milei seeks re-election as a referendum on his libertarian shock therapy, against a Peronist opposition seeking a comeback.

elections.dateNote: Expected Nov or Dec 2027; date not set
elections.stakes: Elects the Assembly of the Representatives of the People, the national legislature, under the presidential system set by the 2022 constitution. The electoral commission has indicated a window but no fixed date.

elections.dateNote: January 2028; exact day not confirmed
elections.seats: President and vice president; 113 Legislative Yuan seats
elections.stakes: Decides whether the ruling DPP keeps the presidency for a second term or power passes to the opposition, with major implications for cross-strait policy. Control of the legislature is also at stake.

elections.dateNote: Due February 2028; exact day not yet set
elections.stakes: Chooses the head of state, who also leads the government in Cyprus's full presidential system. The incumbent has not said whether he will seek re-election, and parties are still choosing candidates.
